The main takeaway from our work is that
the multicommodity flow polytope can be strengthened to obtain good approximation algorithms for many problems, and this strengthening can be done by using a simple rounding technique.

, in many cases, the integrality gap of the multicommodity flow formulation is a good predictor of the performance of the best approximation algorithm for the underlying problem, and the gap between these two numbers is often quite small.
, for many problems, the multicommodity flow linear programming relaxation is a very good relaxation, and the integrality gap is not a good measure of its quality.
